text:
ttps://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/customize-template-files/).

#### Check How Dates Display on Mobile

Mobile visitors often scan headlines quickly and can miss date ranges that only appear in sub-text. Verify that your theme and any customizations clearly display both the start and end dates on smaller screens.

#### Consider Breaking Events Into Sessions or Recurring Events

If your multi-day event is actually a series of separate sessions or workshops, a single multi-day event may not be the right structure. Consider creating a [recurring event](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/recurring-events/) or individual single-day events for each session. This gives attendees a clear per-session view of when to show up.

page_title: Displaying Multiple Calendars by Category
text:
We’re often asked if you can have multiple event calendars on your site. While there isn’t a way to make fully separate calendars on one site, **you can show calendars on multiple pages on your site using Event Calendar Pro’s [tribe_events] shortcode**. To learn how to use this shortcode, check out [the official documentation page](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/calendar-embed-shortcodes/).

You can also use our [event widgets](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/events-calendar-widgets/) to embed event displays in your site’s sidebar, footer, or pages.

page_title: Displaying Multiple Calendars by Category
heading_path: Displaying separate calendars using event categories
text:
## Displaying separate calendars using event categories

You can approximate the *appearance* of having multiple calendars by using Event Categories and linking to category-filtered calendar views.

As an example, let’s say you’re trying to have one event calendar for events in the “Outdoors” category, and then another calendar for events in the “Indoors” category. To make the illusion of each being its own separate calendar, you would do the following steps:

1. Make all “Outdoors” events belong to the “Outdoors” events category.
2. Make all “Indoors” events belong to the “Indoors” events category.
3. Head to Appearance → Menus.
4. Under *Add menu items*, select *Event Categories.*(If you don’t see that option, make sure it is selected in your Screen Options)
5. Add event category links to the event categories you created.
6. Once you add the appropriate menu links to the event categories, click “Save Menu.”

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/event-category-menu-links-example.jpg)

page_title: Displaying Multiple Calendars by Category
heading_path: Displaying separate calendars using event categories
text:
ries, click “Save Menu.”

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/event-category-menu-links-example.jpg)

In this example, you will now have two links in the site’s navigation menu. One will link to “Outdoor Events”, which is **the normal calendar view but only with events in the “Outdoors” category showing**. The other will link to “Indoor Events”, and when clicked will link to the same calendar view, but *only* with events in the “Indoors” category showing. So, while still technically *one* calendar, the different category archive pages make it appear that the Indoors events and Outdoors events exist on separate calendars.

Another great alternative is using the [Filter Bar plugin](https://theeventscalendar.com/products/wordpress-calendar-filter-bar/), which lets you have filters in your main calendar page, and then filter events by Event Category.

You can see a demonstration using the Filter bar on our [demo calendar page](https://demo.theeventscalendar.com/), where the Filter bar is present as the left sidebar on the Events page.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/events-page-category-filter-scaled-1.jpg)

page_title: Using Oxygen Page Builder with The Events Calendar
heading_path: Using Oxygen Page Builder with The Events Calendar
text:
Many of our users use the [Oxygen builder](https://oxygenbuilder.com) and its accompanying theme with our plugins. Sometimes they don’t work together seamlessly, but with a few tweaks, your single event page and your main calendar page will play together nicely with Oxygen.

If you are using our legacy calendar views, make sure to [enable the updated calendar views](https://theeventscalendar.com/knowledgebase/k/enabling-updated-calendar-views/?id=legacyviews) under **Events →** **Settings → Display.**

Next, make sure that you choose the **Default Events Template** option.

![The events display setting page with the Events template option highlighted in red as well as the option to use updated calendar designs when using the oxygen page builder.](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2021-07-12-at-10.08.10-AM.jpg)

From there, you can create a new template with Oxygen and [add the code provided in this handy tutorial on the Oxygen website](https://classic.oxygenbuilder.com/tutorial/how-to-setup-the-events-calendar-with-oxygen/).

page_title: Working with Past Events
text:
When using [The Events Calendar,](https://theeventscalendar.com/) you’ll inevitably accrue several past events. Depending on the needs of your website, you may decide to display these past events for your users to see.

The Events Calendar is set up to focus on current and upcoming events, and by default this is what the main calendar page will show, but the good news is that with a bit of thought, you’ll be able to display your past events for your users. (A note: the month view of our main calendar, by default, displays past events when it displays all events in the current month.)

There are a few different ways to do this, and we’ll show you how along with some other essential things to know about using past events with The Events Calendar.

page_title: Working with Past Events
text:
## Display your past events

You can find your past events on your site at 
```
https://yoursite.com/events/list/?eventDisplay=past
```

If you’d like to display your past events on your site, you can [add a menu item in WordPress](https://theeventscalendar.com/knowledgebase/k/adding-a-calendar-link-to-your-site-menu/) and link your site visitors to your past events directly.

If you have [Events Calendar Pro](https://theeventscalendar.com/products/wordpress-events-calendar/), you can use the [[tribe_events] shortcode](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/calendar-embed-shortcodes/) to display your past events using a past date.
**Please Note:**the past events parameter for shortcodes is only available for Month view, as that article mentions as well.

You can also show past events in reverse order using the snippet provided in [this Knowledgebase article](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/customize-past-events/).

page_title: Working with Past Events
text:
## Importing past events

If you’d like to import past events using our [Event Aggregator service](https://theeventscalendar.com/products/event-aggregator/), by default, these events won’t import. However, if you specify a date parameter, you will be able to get all of your past events imported onto your WordPress site alongside your other events.

Learn more about importing your events in [this Knowledgebase article](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/import-events/).

page_title: Working with Past Events
text:
## Hiding Past Events

By default, when there are no upcoming events, The Events Calendar displays a “Recent Past Events” view to prevent an empty calendar. This feature showcases the most recent past events to keep your calendar populated.

If you wish to hide past events, you can use one of the methods below:

**The Events Calendar Tweaks Extension**

[The Events Calendar Tweaks extension](https://theeventscalendar.com/extensions/the-events-calendar-tweaks/) offers settings to manage past events:​

- **Disable “Recent Past Events”**: Prevents the display of recent past events when no upcoming events are available.​
- **Hide Past Events in Month View**: Removes events from past days in the Month view. Note that this only affects the current month.​

After installing the extension, navigate to **Events > Settings > Tweaks** to configure these options.

**Remove Past Events** **Extension**

page_title: Working with Past Events
text:
extension, navigate to **Events > Settings > Tweaks** to configure these options.

**Remove Past Events** **Extension**

To automatically trash past events after a certain period, install the [Remove Past Events Extension](https://theeventscalendar.com/extensions/remove-past-events/). This extension adds more frequency options for automatically moving past events to the trash. Go to **Events > Settings > General > Maintenance** and select the desired time frame (e.g., 15 minutes, 1 day, 1 week) for removing past events.

This method helps keep your calendar clean by removing outdated events automatically.

Understanding PCI Compliance with Event Tickets
heading_path: Understanding PCI Compliance with Event Tickets
text: This article will help you understand the scope of the rules around Payment Card Industry (PCI) Compliance, how Event Tickets helps with it, what is outside the scope of Event Tickets’s role, and how you can learn more.

page_title: Understanding PCI Compliance with Event Tickets
text:
## What is PCI Compliance?

According to the PCI Security Standards website:

> “The PCI Security Standards Council is a global forum for the ongoing development, enhancement, storage, dissemination and implementation of security standards for account data protection.”

PCI Compliance is centered around preventing fraud, both with customer passwords and details, as well as credit cards. This list of rules and standards reflects how well an organization protects the sensitive data of any person that you collect information from.

page_title: Understanding PCI Compliance with Event Tickets
heading_path: Do I have to be PCI Compliant?
text:
## Do I have to be PCI Compliant?

Anyone who collects sensitive personal information from their site visitors should be aware of compliance. More specifically, if you are transmitting credit card data on your website, your website should be [PCI-DSS](https://blog.pcisecuritystandards.org/topic/pci-dss-v4-0) compliant.

One way to avoid this requirement is to use a third-party system to process payments. A common example of this is to use PayPal Standard to collect and process payment information on your website.

page_title: Understanding PCI Compliance with Event Tickets
heading_path: How do I check my compliance?
text:
## How do I check my compliance?

Get the latest PCI Compliance guidelines on the [Document Library](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/document_library/) of the PCI Security Standards Council website.

There are two documents that would be of most interest to you:

- The latest PCI Compliance DSS (PDF)
- The Self Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) Instructions and Guidelines, which will guide you in selecting the appropriate SAQ document that you should review for your organization.

page_title: Understanding PCI Compliance with Event Tickets
heading_path: Where can I learn more about PCI Compliance?
text:
## Where can I learn more about PCI Compliance?

If you have additional questions regarding PCI Compliance, we highly recommend reaching out directly to the [PCI Security Standards team via their website](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/). We are always happy to [answer any questions](https://theeventscalendar.com/support/) you may have at The Events Calendar, but the PCI Security Standards team specializes in this topic.

page_title: PHP Requirements
text: The minimum required PHP version is 7.4. If you’re using an earlier version, please update to 7.4 or above. We’ve got you covered and can take you through the steps on how to make this change, and will explain*why*this change will be beneficial for all of us.

page_title: PHP Requirements
text:
## What is PHP?

In its simplest terms, PHP is the language that WordPress is written in. PHP acts as the foundation on which your WordPress site is run on, and**the more recent the version of PHP your site uses, the faster and more secure your site will be.**

It’s important to note that PHP versions below 7.4 generally don’t receive security fixes, meaning they’re no longer maintained. PHP 5.6 reached End of Life on December 31st 2018, which marks the official end of support and updates for this version. This could—and often does—leave a site running older versions of PHP vulnerable to hackers.

According to[WordPress.org](https://wordpress.org/support/upgrade-php/), site owners should care about PHP because of the three things they care about the most:

“First, they want their website to work as expected when people visit it—we often call this**site availability**. Second, another major concern is how fast the site loads and functions, or**site performance**. Finally, you likely want your site to make use of all the latest and greatest tools, or**features**.”

page_title: PHP Requirements
heading_path: Why do we have a minimum requirement?
text:
## Why do we have a minimum requirement?

Using a more recent version of PHP will not only help us build a better product—it’ll also help to cut down on support time for outdated PHP versions. This change will furthermore create a better testing environment for us so that we can get bug fixes out more efficiently. These things, along with improved security and performance, will benefit not only our team but our users as well.

With an updated version of PHP, your site can handle more visitors and can run faster than with an outdated version. All of these things will benefit not only our team but our users as well.

page_title: PHP Requirements
heading_path: How do I know what version I’m using?
text:
## How do I know what version I’m using?

You can do this by going to Events → Troubleshooting from the WordPress dashboard and checking out your system information, like in the following screenshot:

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/PHPver.jpg)

**If you’re using PHP version 7.3 or below,**you’ll want to update as soon as possible.

page_title: PHP Requirements
text:
## Using PHP 8.2

The Events Calendar is compatible with PHP 8.2, though you may encounter occasional issues, such as deprecation notices. While these are typically minor, we encourage you to report any PHP version-related issues by submitting a support ticket. This will help us further refine and improve our codebase.

It is worth to mention that deprecation notices and warning messages don’t interrupt the PHP script execution in your website.

While [warning messages](https://phoenixnap.com/kb/php-error-types#PHP_Warning_Error) refer to inclusion of non-existing files, wrong function parameters or incorrect SLQ queries and database connection.

page_title: PHP Requirements
text:
## Deprecation Notices with PHP 8.2

Deprecation notices in PHP are specific types of warnings that are integral to the software development and maintenance process.

Deprecation notices are generated by PHP when it identifies code that uses functions, methods, or practices that will become outdated according to the latest programming standards. These pieces of code are still operational but are marked by the PHP development team to be phased out in future versions.

In short, the notices indicate that, while the code works now, it might become incompatible or cease functioning in upcoming PHP releases.

page_title: PHP Requirements
heading_path: Specific Conditions for Notices to Appear
text:
### Specific Conditions for Notices to Appear

It’s important to note that these deprecation notices only appear when the 
```
wp_debug
```

 constant is enabled in your WordPress configuration.

[https://codex.wordpress.org/WP_DEBUG](https://codex.wordpress.org/WP_DEBUG)

The 
```
wp_debug
```

 mode is a WordPress-specific feature used primarily for development and debugging. When enabled, it displays all PHP errors, warnings, and notices, including deprecations.

This mode is typically turned off on live sites to prevent these technical messages from being visible to users.

You can also learn more about that in the following article: *How to Enable Debugging in WordPress.*

page_title: PHP Requirements
heading_path: Are These Notices a Cause for Concern?
text:
### Are These Notices a Cause for Concern?

Deprecation notices are not bugs or errors in the plugin; they do not indicate immediate problems.

Instead, they serve as **alerts** for developers about code that needs to be updated in future versions. If 
```
wp_debug
```

 is disabled (as recommended for live sites), these notices will not appear, and they will not affect the functionality or performance of your website.

page_title: PHP Requirements
heading_path: Our Approach to Addressing Deprecation Notices
text:
### Our Approach to Addressing Deprecation Notices

We are committed to ensuring our plugin is compatible with the latest PHP standards.

Our development team is aware of these deprecation notices and is proactively working to update the code. This is a routine part of our ongoing efforts to improve the plugin and keep it up-to-date with current technology standards, allowing for timely and efficient code maintenance and enhancement.

page_title: PHP Requirements
text:
### Ensuring Optimal Performance

For most users, especially on live sites with 
```
wp_debug
```

 disabled, these deprecation notices will have no impact as those are not bugs/errors.

However, if you are using *wp_debug* for development purposes and encounter any issues that stop the code from executing and providing the expected result, we encourage you to [contact our support team](https://theeventscalendar.com/support/#contact).

page_title: Plugin Installed but Features Are Missing
category: Plugin Installed But Features Are Missing
heading_path: Plugin Installed but Features Are Missing
text:
If you’ve installed one of our premium plugins but some features are missing or not working as expected, then this is often a quick fix. Below are the two most common reasons for this issue and how to resolve them.

---

page_title: Plugin Installed but Features Are Missing
category: Plugin Installed But Features Are Missing
heading_path: 1. Make Sure the Plugin Is Activated
text:
## 1. Make Sure the Plugin Is Activated

Sometimes, the plugin may be installed but not actually active on your site.

page_title: Plugin Installed but Features Are Missing
category: Plugin Installed But Features Are Missing
heading_path: How to check if the plugin is activated:
text:
### How to check if the plugin is activated:

1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to **Plugins > Installed Plugins**.
2. Look for the name of the plugin you installed.
3. If you see an **“Activate”** link under the plugin name, it means the plugin is currently **inactive**.
4. Click **Activate**.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-4-scaled-1.jpg)

> For our premium features to work, the plugin must be active. Repeat this for any related plugins that we offer.

---

page_title: Plugin Installed but Features Are Missing
category: Plugin Installed But Features Are Missing
text:
## 2. Check for Version Compatibility

Our plugins are designed to work together as a suite. If one plugin has been updated but others haven’t, this can cause features to disappear or break.

page_title: Plugin Installed but Features Are Missing
category: Plugin Installed But Features Are Missing
text:
### Why this happens:

When we release an update, the **common code shared across our plugins** may change. To ensure compatibility, all related plugins need to be updated to the latest version at the same time. Running mismatched versions can result in features not showing up, even if the plugin is active.

page_title: Plugin Installed but Features Are Missing
category: Plugin Installed But Features Are Missing
heading_path: How to check and fix version issues:
text:
### How to check and fix version issues:

1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to **Plugins > Installed Plugins**.
2. Look for any of our plugins that say **“Update Available”** and note which versions are currently active.
3. Update **all plugins in our suite** to the latest versions.
- You can update them by clicking the **“Update now”** link next to each plugin.
4. Once all plugins are updated, refresh your site or plugin settings page to see if the missing features appear.

> You may also see a notice in your dashboard prompting you to update multiple plugins together — make sure to follow it if you do.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-5-6.jpg)

---

page_title: Plugin Installed but Features Are Missing
category: Plugin Installed But Features Are Missing
text:
## Still not seeing the features?

If the plugin is active and all related plugins are updated, but you’re still missing features:

- Clear your [site and browser cache.](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/how-to-clear-your-site-and-browser-cache-properly/)
- Check for [plugin conflicts](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/testing-for-conflicts/) by deactivating other non-related plugins temporarily.
- Contact our support team with your [system information](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/sharing-your-system-information/), and we’ll help you troubleshoot further.

page_title: Managing Your Power Automate Endpoints
text:
Do you have a lot of flows and want more tools to manage them?

Good news, you can easily monitor your Power Automate endpoints (triggers and actions used by your connectors) via the Power Automate Endpoint Dashboard.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screenshot-2023-12-07-at-09-59-31-Settings-‹-The-Events-Calendar-Complete-Collection-—-WordPress.jpg)

page_title: Managing Your Power Automate Endpoints
text:
### How you get there

1. Go to Events > Settings > Integrations OR Tickets > Settings > Integrations
2. Scroll down the page until you get to the Power Automate Endpoint Dashboard

page_title: Managing Your Power Automate Endpoints
text:
### How the dashboard works

As you can see from the screenshot above, the Dashboard lists all endpoints available for [The Events Calendar](https://powerautomate.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/details/shared_theeventscalendar/the-events-calendar/) and [Event Tickets](https://powerautomate.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/details/shared_eventtickets/event-tickets/) Power Automate connectors.

Each of those endpoints matches the name of a Power Automate trigger or action for The Events Calendar and Event Tickets connectors.

Listed with each endpoint are …

- **Name**: endpoint name
- **Last Access:**name of the app last used to access that endpoint with the date and time of last access
- **Queue**: the number of unprocessed flows queued for the corresponding endpoint
- **Actions**:
- *Clear Queue*: wipes the queue for that endpoint clean
- *Disable/Enable:* lets you enable or disable a specific endpoint
- e.g. to prevent misuse/access to an endpoint that you are not using
- e.g. use as a makeshift “panic button”

page_title: Automating Events and Tickets with Microsoft Power Automate
heading_path: Automating Events and Tickets with Microsoft Power Automate
text:
Now you can use [Microsoft Power Automate (MSPA)](https://powerautomate.microsoft.com/) to combine [The Events Calendar Pro](https://theeventscalendar.com/products/wordpress-events-calendar/) and [Event Tickets Plus](https://theeventscalendar.com/products/wordpress-event-tickets/) with many of your favorite third-party apps and tools. MSPA allows you to integrate our plugins by using what they call “flows”. A flow is a workflow that sets up an automation between two different apps.

**Useful Links:**

- [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/powerplatform/power-automate)
- [List of connectors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/connector-reference/connector-reference-powerautomate-connectors)
- Go through the first 2 sections of [Get started with Power Automate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/get-started-flows/) (18 minutes)
- Take the [Assessment](https://powerautomate.microsoft.com/en-gb/automation-solutions/) to get recommendations of helpful flows

To explain how this works, we’ll be creating an actual automation! In this example, every time you publish an event (trigger), an email will be sent to someone using Gmail.

- Etc..

text:
### Mapping Dynamic Fields

The trigger and the operation connectors are now linked. But we are not done! We need to teach the action app how to use the trigger app’s data. This needs to be done one field at a time. For a full reference of every available trigger, action, and dynamic field, see [this article](#).

In the action app’s connector (Gmail in this example):

- Review every field available under the *Parameters* tab to see if they require mapping 
- You might need to click on a *Show All* link to see them

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-9.jpg)

- For each field you review:
1. Ask yourself if that field needs to receive information from your trigger (The Events Calendar)
2. When you find a field needing information from your trigger, click on it to select it.
3. Click on the lightning bolt icon that appears to display the available dynamic fields from the trigger

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-10.jpg)

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-11-1024x519-1.jpg)

1. Repeat this process for every available field until you are satisfied

heading_path: Priority support through the TEC Help Hub
text:
Working on your site and need some help? You can chat with our AI chatbot or get connected to a live human from our support team, right from within your WordPress Dashboard. Under **Events > Help > Support Hub**, you’ll see some different options depending on whether or not you have an active license and have given consent to telemetry.

Our chatbot is available for all users, no license required. This bot is thoroughly trained on our knowledgebase and can answer many different types of questions ranging from what features are available and how they can be set up to troubleshooting issues you may be experiencing. It’s also available to help immediately, 24/7/365.

Our support team is here to help via live chat 8am – 5pm ET Monday – Friday for our active license-holders. If you need help outside of these hours or a chat agent is not available during this time (for instance, if the chat queue is full), you can also submit a ticket to our support team from the Support Hub. We will review your ticket and follow up with you ASAP.

From the Profile screen you can update your name, email address, and password.

![The Promoter profile screen showing fields for name, email address, and password](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/select-next-website-promoter.jpg)

💡 Changing your password requires entering your current password first, to protect your account.

If you change your email address here, note that this also changes the email address used to log in to Promoter. A verification email will be sent to the new address, and the new address won’t take effect until you click the verification link. See [Verifying and Changing Your Send-From Email Address](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/promoter-email/) for more detail on how email changes work.

page_title: Managing Your Promoter Account and Data
text:
## Data Requests and Account Deletion

The Events Calendar does not offer a self-service account deletion option inside Promoter. To request export or deletion of your account data, use the [data request form](https://theeventscalendar.com/data-request/). The sections below explain what data is held, how it is handled, and your rights under GDPR.

When subscribed to our products or services, you are on a monthly or annual renewal [Agreement](https://theeventscalendar.com/terms/) and can cancel at any time.

page_title: Managing Your Promoter Account and Data
text:
### What Personal Data Is Held

We only retain records necessary to provide you with our products and services. The account information we store includes:

- Name
- Email address
- Billing address
- IP address for transactional purchases as well as marketing and re-marketing purposes
- Payment method information
- Account username and an encrypted account password
- License keys assigned to your account
- Support threads opened in our forums
- Emails related to your purchases
- Support emails you have initiated

page_title: Managing Your Promoter Account and Data
text:
### Exporting or Deleting Your Data

You can submit a request to export or delete your data at any time using our [data request form](https://theeventscalendar.com/data-request/). Once data has been deleted and/or anonymized, this action cannot be reversed.

page_title: Managing Your Promoter Account and Data
heading_path: Where Data Is Stored and Processed
text:
### Where Data Is Stored and Processed

All data is currently stored and processed in the United States.

page_title: Managing Your Promoter Account and Data
text:
### How Data Is Deleted

We delete and anonymize any and all records that we are legally able to upon your request. Please note that once this has been done, there is no option to reverse the decision.

page_title: Managing Your Promoter Account and Data
text:
### Data Protection

We encrypt as much data as possible and have multiple security measures in place, including limited access for our own team members.

page_title: Managing Your Promoter Account and Data
text:
### Third Parties

The Events Calendar shares as little data as possible with third parties outside of our organization. See our [Privacy Policy](https://theeventscalendar.com/privacy-policy/) for full details on our data practices.

page_title: Managing Your Promoter Account and Data
text:
### Data Access

Access to data is limited based on company discipline — team members only have access to the data needed to execute their specific duties. We also use two-factor authorization and other measures to ensure appropriate access controls.

heading_path: Verifying and Changing Your Send-From Email Address in Promoter
text:
Promoter lets you use any email address to send messages. As long as you are the rightful owner of that address, of course.

Unless you specify otherwise, Promoter will send messages from the email address you used while setting up your Promoter account.

**Important note:**until you can confirm ownership of that email address, Promoter will not allow you to send or schedule messages.

page_title: Verifying and Changing Your Send-From Email Address in Promoter
text:
## Verifying Your Email Address

As you probably already know, immediately after setting up your Promoter account you should have received a “Verify Email Address for Promoter” email (see screenshot below).

Confirming ownership of that email address is pretty straightforward: simply click on the *Verify Email* button.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/verify.png)

Once you click on the blue button, you will automatically be brought back to your Promoter account where you will be met with a success message and you should be all done!

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/thanks.png)

**Important note:**the verification email is time-sensitive, so you might have to send a new one if you wait too long. If your Verification Email is expired, you can re-send by hitting the *Update Settings* from your [Promoter profile](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/promoter-account/) page.

If you are not using Promoter, you can bump into that error message if you have entered a license key into the Promoter field on the *Events → Settings → Licenses* page by accident. The warning will be displayed again on the next page load, even if you have dismissed it before.

This can be fixed with a little snippet for which we recommend using the [Code Snippets](https://wordpress.org/plugins/code-snippets/) plugin. (Make sure to check out our [related article](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/code-snippets/), too.)

Here is how to go about fixing this:

1. Create a database backup first! – This is always important before making any changes in your database.
2. Create a new snippet with Code Snippets, and copy-paste the below code.
3. Set it as “Only run once”. (See screenshot below.)
4. Click on “Save Changes”. (Not “Save Changes and Execute Once”!)
5. Go to *Snippets → All Snippets*.
6. Click on the play icon next to the snippet to run it once.
7. The relevant entry from the database should be removed and the notice will disappear.

Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
heading_path: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text: This article covers everything involved in creating, styling, sending, and monitoring messages in Promoter — from configuring your email template through to reading the results after a message is sent.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
## Scheduled Messages

Click into the event you want to create a message for, then click the **Create Message** button. You’ll be presented with two options: a scheduled message and a trigger-based message. Select **Scheduled Message**.

![The message type selector in Promoter showing Scheduled Message and Trigger-Based Message options](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2022-07-06-at-8.24.35-AM.jpg)

The message editor will open. Work through the following fields:

#### Admin Title

Enter an internal title for the message. This is recommended but not required — it helps you identify messages in the event dashboard.

![The admin title field in the Promoter message editor](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/admin-title.png)

#### Audience

Choose who will receive this message. The dropdown lets you select one or more audiences:

- The attendee lists for this event (people who purchased a ticket or registered for the event)
- The attendee lists of other events
- Your [custom lists](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/customize-attendee-list/)

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
ts of other events
- Your [custom lists](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/customize-attendee-list/)

![The audience selector in the Promoter message editor](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/audience.png)

#### Sender

Set the name and email address that appears in the reply-to line of the email. By default this uses the name and email of your Promoter account.

![The sender name and email fields in the Promoter message editor](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/sending.png)

💡 If you are using your own domain for sending emails, the “From” email is taken from your [Mail Delivery Settings](https://theeventscalendar.com/knowledgebase/mail-delivery-settings-and-domain-verification-for-promoter/), while the “Reply-To” email defaults to your Promoter account email.

#### Message Content

Enter the subject line and body of the email. You can style the message, create hyperlinks, add buttons, and insert images.

![The message content editor in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/customize.png)

#### Merge Tags

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
message content editor in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/customize.png)

#### Merge Tags

Use merge tags to insert dynamic content — such as the attendee’s name or the event title — directly into your message. See the [Merge Tags guide](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/event-categories-tags/) for the full list of available tags.

![The merge tags panel in the Promoter message editor](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-35.png)

#### Schedule

Once you’ve created a message and are ready to send it, you have two options.

#### Schedule for Later

To queue a message for a specific date and time, set the date and time you want it to go out and click **Schedule**.

![The Schedule for later date and time picker in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/schedule-later.png)

Once emails enter the queue at the email-sending service, the exact send time is handled by that service. On occasion there can be minor delays, but on average sending is fast.

#### Send Immediately

Click the **Send Now** button to send the message right away.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
s, but on average sending is fast.

#### Send Immediately

Click the **Send Now** button to send the message right away.

![The Send Now button in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/send-now.png)

After clicking Send Now, you still need to confirm before the message actually goes out — this prevents accidental sends. Select **Yes** from the “Send This Message” dropdown and click **Confirm**.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
### Cancel a Scheduled Message

Scheduled messages can be canceled any time before they are sent.

1. From the Events dashboard, click on the event. ![The Promoter Events dashboard showing upcoming events](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/upcoming-events.png)
2. Click the title of the scheduled message you want to cancel. ![The messages list for a single event in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/messages.png)
3. Scroll to the bottom of the message detail and click **Cancel Scheduling**. This immediately removes the schedule and returns the message to Draft status. ![The Cancel Scheduling link at the bottom of the message detail in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/delivery.png)

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
### Message Statuses

Scheduled messages have four possible statuses:

1. **Draft** — The message has been saved but not yet sent or scheduled. You can return to it at any time to continue editing. ![Draft status label on a Promoter message](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/draft.png)
2. **Scheduled** — The message is queued to be sent at the chosen date and time. ![Scheduled status label on a Promoter message](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/scheduled.png)
3. **Processing** — The message is actively being sent to the selected audiences and lists. Depending on the size of the audience, it may remain in this status for a short while. ![Processing status label on a Promoter message](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/processing.png)
4. **Sent** — The message has been sent successfully. You can celebrate 🙂 ![Sent status label on a Promoter message](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/sent.png)

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
## Triggered Messages

Wouldn’t it be nice if there was a way to automatically send a message to an attendee that performs a specific action (e.g.: purchases a ticket)? If that piques your interest, then Promoter’s **triggered messages** featured might be for you. Triggered messages are messages that are sent when some action takes place, letting Promoter handle the heavy lifting for you.

Let’s see how it works.

First, click and select the event that you’d like to add a triggered message to. You’ll then see options to create a new message or create a trigger. Go ahead and select the **Triggered Message** option.

![Triggered messages with Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2022-07-06-at-10.06.57-AM.jpg)

#### Title

Promoter will ask you to add a title for the message. This is for your eyes only to help you distinguish it from other messages. Your recipients will not see it.

![Add a title for your triggered message](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/admin-title.jpg)

#### Select a Trigger

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-17-2.png)

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
2026/06/admin-title.jpg)

#### Select a Trigger

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-17-2.png)

Next up, Promoter needs to know when it should send the message. There are currently four options to choose from:

- **Ticket purchased:**Sends a message to the purchaser as soon as the attendee is created in The Events Calendar. This applies to tickets created in WordPress with Tribe Commerce or Event Tickets Plus. Note, the triggered message will only be sent to the purchaser. It will NOT be sent to any additional attendees.
- **Event Check-in:** Sends a message as soon as the attendee checks into the event. This is kind of a neat way to welcome guests to the event or send them a note that gives them what they need to enjoy the event. The message is sent to the purchaser.
- **RSVP Going:** Sends a message when an attendee RSVPs that they are going to the event.
- **RSVP Not Going:** Sends a message when an attendee RSVPs that they are not going to the event.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
e going to the event.
- **RSVP Not Going:** Sends a message when an attendee RSVPs that they are not going to the event.

Note that only one trigger can be assigned to a message. It’s also worth noting that triggered messages do not replace the transactional emails that Event Tickets and Event Tickets Plus send confirming their registration.

Once you select a Trigger, **Promoter will automatically select the appropriate audience** for you.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-18-2.png)

#### Customize Your Message

There are a couple of options to do this.

The first is to use one of the pre-written content shortcut messages in Promoter.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-10-6.png)

This will expedite the process by populating the subject line and body content for you instead of having to write it yourself. Oh, and you can even [create your own content shortcuts](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/promoter-shortcuts-campaigns/)!

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
create your own content shortcuts](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/promoter-shortcuts-campaigns/)!

The second option is to manually write a message. In this case, you will enter the subject line and the content for the message. You can style the message, create hyperlinks, add buttons and insert images in the content area.

💡 **Pro tip:** you can use [merge tags](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/event-categories-tags/) (dynamically populated content)

![Add merge tags to your triggered messages](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/merge-tags.jpg)

#### Activate the Triggered Message

Once everything is configured, it’s time to click the “Activate trigger” button and let Promoter handle things from there!

![activate triggered messages by clicking on the button](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-5-3.jpg)

#### Viewing Triggered Messages

There are a couple of different ways to see all of your triggered messages in Promoter. The first is in the Messages section of the event.

![View triggered messages here](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-7-1.jpg)

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
ection of the event.

![View triggered messages here](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-7-1.jpg)

Trigger-based messages are easy to recognize as they have a little lightning icon next to them. You can edit or deactivate a trigger by clicking on the message title.

The second way to view your triggered messages is in the Timeline section of the event. This provides visualization for when emails are scheduled to send for the selected event.

![A triggered message for a selected event](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-8.jpg)

The number in the little circle next to the name of a triggered message indicates the number of times the message has been sent for the selected event.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
### Message Statuses

Triggered messages have two possible statuses:

1. **Trigger Active** — Promoter will automatically send the message to any attendee who performs the associated trigger action. For example, if the trigger is set to “Ticket Purchased,” the message is sent to every attendee who buys a ticket while the trigger is active. ![A triggered message showing Trigger Active status in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-12-1024x279-1.png) ![The trigger active status in the Promoter messages list](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-14-1024x293-1.png)
2. **Trigger Inactive** — Promoter will not send the message while this status is set. Use this to temporarily pause a triggered message without deleting it. ![A triggered message showing Trigger Inactive status in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-12-1024x279-1.png) 💡 Triggered messages are not retroactive. Attendees who performed the trigger action while the message was set to Trigger Inactive will not receive the message when it is switched back to Trigger Active.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
## Merge Tags

Merge tags are dynamic fields that allow you to customize the content of a message. For example, let’s say that you want to include the first name of the attendee, the title of the event and the number of days left until the event begins in your message. You can simply use the “Attendee First Name”, “Event Title” and “Days Until Event” merge tags to do so. As the message is sent out, each merge tag will be dynamically replaced with the desired information.

Merge tags are available for every aspect of an event: Event details, Virtual Event, Venue Details, Tickets information, Attendee Data, etc. Merge Tags are located to the right of the message subject line and message body.

****

![Screenshot at October 22nd 2020 - 2.32.25 am.png](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/4QNuFw.png)

To add a merge tag to a message, place the cursor exactly where you want the tag to appear in the message and click on the desired tag. The merge tag will now display in the message editor.****

#### Previewing Merge Tags

It’s always a good idea to preview a message to make sure everything looks good.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
ditor.****

#### Previewing Merge Tags

It’s always a good idea to preview a message to make sure everything looks good.

Use the Preview link at the top of the Message Editor to see what your message will look like. Merge tags will be replaced by brackets to give you a sense of where the data will go.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/preview.png)

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
### Events Merge Tags

The merge tags in this section include details about the event you are sending a message for.

| Merge Tag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Event Title | Adds the title of the event to the message. |
| Event Excerpt | Includes the WordPress excerpt for the event. If no excerpt is defined for the event, this tag will use the excerpt automatically generated by WordPress. |
| Event Start Date | Adds the date the event is scheduled to begin. E.g. July 15 |
| Event Start Time | Adds the time of day that the event is scheduled to begin. E.g. 10:00 a.m. |
| Event End Date | Adds the date the event is scheduled to end. E.g. July 16 |
| Event End Time | Adds the time of day that the event is scheduled to begin. E.g. 10:00 a.m. |
| Event URL | Adds the web address (URL) of the event to the message. E.g. your-website.com/link-to-event |

#### Location (Venue)

The merge tags in this section provide details about the location of the event.

| Merge Tag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Location Name | Displays the name of the venue, if one is available. |
| Venue Address | Displays the physical address of the location, as provided by the site. |

#### Virtual Events

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
able. |
| Venue Address | Displays the physical address of the location, as provided by the site. |

#### Virtual Events

| Merge Tag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Event Online | Adds “Livestream” when you have a virtual event. |
| Zoom ID | Adds the Zoom ID of your Virtual Event. E.g. 657 082 0943 |
| Zoom URL | Adds the Zoom URL of your Virtual Event. E.g. https://zoom.us/j/6590830921?pwd=ODNORDBVK5JwdDE3Unp2RnUrc2hqdz06 |
| Zoom Password | Adds the Zoom password of your Virtual Event. E.g. opensesame |

| Video URL | Adds the URL to your live event (e.g.: FB live or Youtube – https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b5ANAR7bIZA) |

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
### Tickets Merge Tags

The merge tags in this section contain information about the tickets created for the event using the Event Tickets and/or Event Tickets Plus plugin.

If you have several tickets for an event, each ticket will get dedicated merge tags. For example, if you have one ticket called Early Bird and another ticket called General Admission, you will have the following options for the Ticket Name merge tag:

- Ticket Name (Early Bird)
- Ticket Name (General Admission)

| Merge Tag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Buy Now Link | Adds a direct link to the ticket form on the event page of your website. |
| Ticket Name | Adds the name of the ticket. |
| Ticket Price | Displays the price of a ticket for the event.
Important note: the currency is not included in the output. As such, you will want to make sure to include it before or after the merge tag, depending on the currency. |
| Tickets Remaining | Displays the quantity of tickets that are left to purchase for the event for a particular ticket.
For example, if you have a ticket that has 100 tickets available and 90 tickets have been purchased, once the message is sent the merge tag will be dynamically replaced by “10” i

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
ilable and 90 tickets have been purchased, once the message is sent the merge tag will be dynamically replaced by “10” in the message. |

#### Attendees

The merge tags in this section provide details about the attendee receiving the sent message.

| Merge Tag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Attendee First Name | Adds the first name of the attendee receiving the message. |
| Attendee Last Name | Adds the last name of the attendee receiving the message. |
| Attendee Email | Adds the email address of the attendee receiving the message. |
| Attendee Ticket Type | Adds the name of the ticket the attendee has purchased. For example, if the attendee purchased a ticket called “General Admission,” then that will be the name that is displayed in the message. |

**Note:** At this time, Event Tickets does not have merged tags enabled, so the name field contains both the first and last names by default. However, once your contacts are in Promoter, you will have access to merge tags for first and last names separately.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
## Delete a Message

To permanently delete a message, click the **Delete** link at the top of the message editor and confirm when prompted.

![The Delete link at the top of the Promoter message editor](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2022-07-06-at-10.14.45-AM.jpg)

⚠️ Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. If you only need to stop the message from going out rather than remove it entirely, use Cancel Scheduling instead.

page_title: Creating Scheduled and Triggered Messages in Promoter
text:
## Message Reports

Promoter tracks how many times emails have been opened and how many times links inside them have been clicked. The event-level view shows aggregate totals across all messages sent for that event.

![The Promoter event-level report showing total opens and clicks across all messages for an event](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/opened-emails.png)

Click into the event title to see a report broken down by individual message.

![The per-message report view in Promoter showing opens and clicks for each individual message](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/reports.png)

For more on how Promoter tracks link clicks — including why links change appearance in received emails and how to disable tracking — see [Promoter Tracking Links](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/promoter-tracking-links/).

## How to Test Promoter Messages Before Sending

Ensuring that your email communications to event attendees are correctly formatted and fully functional is crucial. Despite previews and test emails often providing a good indication of how your message will appear, some issues may only become apparent in the actual emails received by attendees.

This guide outlines a straightforward method for testing Promoter emails, allowing you to experience them just as an attendee would.

#### Step 1: Creating an Unofficial Test Email

Before sending the official email to your attendees, it’s advisable to conduct a test with an “unofficial” version of your email. This process involves the following steps:

1. **Create a Custom List in Promoter:** Start by creating a [Promoter custom list](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/customize-attendee-list/). Add only the recipients you wish to test the email with, ensuring this list is exclusively used for testing purposes.
2. **Duplicate the Scheduled Message:** Identify the [scheduled message](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/promoter-messages/) you intend to test. Duplicate this message and select your newly created custom list as the sole recipient. It is crucial to ensure that this message is only sent to the custom list to prevent accidental dispatch to your entire attendee list.
3. **Incorporate Test Links:** To effectively test the “Clicks” tracking functionality, include test links within your email. This step is vital to ensure all links within your email are functioning correctly and tracking engagement as intended.
4. **Send the Test Email:** Once you have completed the setup, click the “Send Now” button. Await the arrival of the email in your designated mailbox to procee

#### Step 2: Evaluating the Test Email

Upon receiving the test email, conduct a thorough inspection to assess its appearance and functionality:

- **Check Email Formatting:** Examine the email’s layout, text formatting, and visual elements to ensure everything displays as expected across different devices and email clients.
- **Verify Link Functionality:** Click on all links within the email to confirm they are working correctly and directing to the intended destinations.

#### Step 3: Troubleshooting

If, during your evaluation, you encounter issues with link functionality or other aspects of the email, immediate action is required:

- **Contact Support:** Reach out to the [Help Desk](https://theeventscalendar.com/support/#contact) for assistance in resolving any detected problems. Provide detailed information about the issues encountered to facilitate a swift resolution.

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text: Promoter includes two features for reusing message configurations across events: **shortcuts** and **campaigns**. Shortcuts are individual reusable message templates. Campaigns are collections of shortcuts that can be applied to an event all at once. This article covers both.

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
## Promoter Shortcuts

A shortcut is a message template you can use to quickly create emails over and over again. With a shortcut, you pre-define:

- **Subject line and message content** — copy and [merge tags](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/event-categories-tags/)
- **Default audience** — attendees of this event, or attendees of all events
- **Scheduling** (optional) — when the message will be sent relative to the event’s date, start time, or end time

For example, instead of manually writing a reminder to attendees 3 days before every event, you can use the “Event Reminder” shortcut. In one click, your reminder is ready to go.

Shortcuts are accessible from two places:

**From the Shortcuts menu** — there is a link to your shortcuts in the main Promoter navigation.

![The Shortcuts link in the Promoter main navigation menu](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/shortcuts-menu.png)

**From the message editor** — shortcuts are also accessible while creating a new message.

![The shortcuts panel accessible from within the Promoter message editor](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/new-message.png)

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
### Working with Shortcuts

The Shortcuts page lists Promoter’s twelve default shortcuts.

![The Promoter Shortcuts page showing the twelve default shortcuts](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/twelve.png)

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
### Default Shortcut Actions

Each default shortcut supports the following actions:

![The action menu for a default shortcut in Promoter showing Preview, Edit, Duplicate, and Add to event options](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/default-shortcut-actions.png)

- **Preview** — View the shortcut’s message before using it.
- **Edit** (aka Customize) — Modify the shortcut’s content, audience, or schedule.
- **Duplicate** — Create a copy of the shortcut as a starting point for a custom version, without modifying the original.
- **Add to event** — Automatically schedule the pre-written message for selected events.

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
### Creating Custom Shortcuts

Custom shortcuts can be created in one of three ways from the Shortcuts page:

![The Create Custom Shortcut block on the Promoter Shortcuts page](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/promoter-create-shortcut.png)

1. Click the **Create Custom Shortcut** block to start from scratch.
2. Select **Edit** from a default shortcut’s action menu to customize that default shortcut directly.
3. Select **Duplicate** from a default shortcut’s action menu to create a custom copy.

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
### Custom Shortcut Actions

Custom shortcuts support the same four actions as default shortcuts, plus two additional ones:

![The action menu for a custom shortcut in Promoter, showing the additional Delete and Revert options](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/promoter-shortcuts-actions.png)

- **Delete** — Permanently removes a custom shortcut. Applies only to shortcuts created from scratch or duplicated from a default.
- **Revert** — Undoes any customization applied to a default shortcut, restoring it to its original factory settings. Applies only to default shortcuts that were edited.

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
## Promoter Campaigns

A campaign is a reusable collection of shortcuts that you can assign to an event in one step. Rather than adding shortcuts to an event one at a time, a campaign lets you apply a curated set of messages — your pre-event reminder, day-of message, post-event follow-up, and so on — all at once.

#### Creating a Campaign

Head to the Shortcuts page and expand the **Create a campaign** sidebar.

![The Create a Campaign sidebar expanded on the Promoter Shortcuts page](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-1024x553-1.png)

Shortcuts can be added to a campaign in one of two ways:

1. **Manually selecting shortcuts** — choose the shortcuts you use most often.
2. **Using the starter campaign** — a set of commonly used default shortcuts for a successful event promotion (the default shortcuts can be modified).

![The two campaign creation options: manually select shortcuts or use the starter campaign](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-2-1024x573-1.png)

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
### Manually Selecting Shortcuts

Click **Add a Shortcut to this campaign**. The screen will switch to Shortcut Adding Mode. Click the large plus (+) icon on any shortcut to add it to the campaign. When you’re done with your selection, click **Save** to exit Shortcut Adding Mode.

**Pro tips:**

- Campaigns require a minimum of two shortcuts.
- The default audience and schedule (if any) are shown in each shortcut box to help you decide which ones to include.

![Shortcut Adding Mode in Promoter showing shortcuts with plus icons to add them to a campaign](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-3-1024x496-1.png)

![A campaign taking shape with several shortcuts added](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-4-1024x503-1.png)

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
### Using the Starter Campaign

Click **Check out our Starter Campaign** to preview the suggested shortcuts. Click **Add Shortcuts** once you’ve reviewed them. You can remove any suggested shortcut after adding it.

![The Starter Campaign preview in Promoter showing the suggested shortcuts](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-5-1024x595-1.png)

![A campaign created from the Starter Campaign with shortcuts added](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-6-1024x475-1.png)

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
text:
### Removing Shortcuts from a Campaign

You can remove a shortcut from a campaign at any time by clicking its contextual menu and selecting **Remove from campaign**.

![The contextual menu on a shortcut within a campaign, showing the Remove from campaign option](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-7-3.png)

Save the campaign when you’re done. Additional shortcuts can be added at any time by clicking **Add a Shortcut to this campaign**.

page_title: Creating Promoter Shortcuts and Campaigns
heading_path: Applying a Campaign to an Event
text:
### Applying a Campaign to an Event

Campaigns are designed to be applied to events. To add a campaign to an event:

1. Navigate to the event of your choice.
2. Click the **Add Your Campaign** option.

![The Add Your Campaign option on an event in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-13-1024x327-1.png)

![The campaign selection screen in Promoter](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-14-1024x504-1.png)

You’ll be taken to a confirmation screen. Review your shortcut selections carefully before proceeding — you can still adjust them at this step.

![The campaign confirmation screen in Promoter showing the shortcuts that will be applied to the event](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-16-1024x578-1.png)

After confirming, you’ll see a list of messages that were created as a result of adding the campaign to the event. All messages are set to Draft status and won’t send until they have been published. You can still undo the campaign at this stage by removing the messages from the Messages screen.

heading_path: Applying a Campaign to an Event
text:
ey have been published. You can still undo the campaign at this stage by removing the messages from the Messages screen.

![The messages list for an event after a campaign has been applied, showing all messages in Draft status](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-17-1024x583-1.png)

page_title: Understanding Link Tracking in Promoter Emails
heading_path: Understanding Link Tracking in Promoter Emails
text:
Once you connect your website to Promoter and set up your [Mail Deliverability](https://theeventscalendar.com/knowledgebase/mail-delivery-settings-and-domain-verification-for-promoter/), you’ll be ready to send messages to your attendees using Promoter.

During this setup process, you need to add some new entries to your DNS like new CNAME and TXT records. Those records have different functions and one of their functions is to track the clicks your message receives. By doing this, the Promoter can tell you how many people have opened your email, how many have clicked on the link you shared inside the message, etc.

page_title: Understanding Link Tracking in Promoter Emails
text:
## Changing Links

If you try to inspect the link once you receive a message from Promoter, you’ll notice that the link is different from what you used when you created the message using Promoter Dashboard. **This is expected, don’t worry!**

Under the hook, the Promoter creates brand new links for your message and adds some parameters to ensure that each message’s link will be unique.

This is what allows the Promoter to track the clicks you receive. Every time a user clicks on one of those links, they will be redirected to the exact address that you used when you created the message. Promoter uses this redirection to make a count of how many clicks your messages are receiving.

page_title: Understanding Link Tracking in Promoter Emails
text:
## Are There Any Risks Involved?

Short answer: **No**.

This is a normal behavior from many mailing systems, even if you use Gmail or any other system that lets you know once the user has received/read the message or provides any metrics this is what they’re using under the hook.

page_title: Understanding Link Tracking in Promoter Emails
text:
## How to Disable It?

Promoter Dashboard doesn’t offer a setting focused on that. So far, the CNAME entry in your DNS is the one responsible for tracking.

If you don’t want to track your messages, remove this entry from your DNS.
But, keep in mind that the Promoter will be unable to tell you how many messages have been delivered, opened or which links have more clicks.

page_title: Understanding Link Tracking in Promoter Emails
heading_path: Links from Promoter Emails Display “Your Connection is Not Secure”
text:
## Links from Promoter Emails Display “Your Connection is Not Secure”

If links in your Promoter emails are showing a “Your connection is not secure” message, this issue is often related to the SSL certificate for the domain added in the [Mail Delivery Settings](https://theeventscalendar.com/knowledgebase/mail-delivery-settings-and-domain-verification-for-promoter/) page. In some cases, the SSL certificate might not have been generated correctly, which results in this error when users click on the email links.

To fix this, please follow these steps:

1. Reach out to our [Help Desk](https://theeventscalendar.com/support/#contact) for assistance.
2. Provide them with details of the issue, including the domain you’ve configured in the Mail Delivery Settings.
3. The support team will ensure the missing SSL certificate is properly generated and applied.

Once the SSL certificate is correctly installed, the issue should be resolved, and the links in your Promoter emails will no longer display the “Your connection is not secure” message.

page_title: How to Show Event Content Only to Attendees
heading_path: How to Show Event Content Only to Attendees
text:
The Event Tickets Protected Content shortcodes allow you to display content on any WordPress page or post to certain users if they are logged in and whether or not they have registered for a given event, or registered for a specific type of ticket or RSVP.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/etp-shortcode-protected-content-1024x953-1.png)The first shortcode will display for users who are logged in and have registered for the event with ID 123. The second shortcode will display for users who have not registered for the event.

page_title: How to Show Event Content Only to Attendees
text:
## What it’s good for

There are times when you might want to show content to specific users. For example, let’s say you’re creating a page on your site that promotes one of your events that contains either tickets or RSVPs. Protected content can be useful for many things, including:

- Displaying a livestream video only to users who have registered for the event.
- Sharing links or other resources to users who have registered for the event.
- Showing a promotional video if the user has not registered for the event.
- Providing coupon codes as an incentive for users who have not registered for the event.

page_title: How to Show Event Content Only to Attendees
text:
## Requirements

Both Event Tickets and the [Event Tickets Plus add-on](https://theeventscalendar.com/wordpress-event-tickets/) are required to use the Ticket and RSVP Protected Content shortcodes.

page_title: How to Show Event Content Only to Attendees
text:
## Basic usage

For tickets:

```
[tribe_tickets_protected_content post_id="123"]
Your content
[/tribe_tickets_protected_content]
```

For RSVPs:

```
[tribe_tickets_rsvp_protected_content post_id="123"]
Your content
[/tribe_tickets_rsvp_protected_content]
```

page_title: How to Show Event Content Only to Attendees
text:
## Parameters

Both shortcodes accept the following parameters to control the visibility of content:

- ```
post_id
```

 (Required) – The ID of the event, page or post where the ticket or RSVP is created.
- ```
on
```

 – Sets the date and time that the protected content should start to display. Use 
```
event_start_date
```

 to display the protected content when the event starts. Otherwise, provide the specific date and time in 
```
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
```

 format (e.g. 2020-06-01 07:00:00 for June 1, 2020 at 7:00 am). Default = empty.

The 
```
[tribe_tickets_protected_content]
```

shortcode takes three additional parameters:

- ```
ticket_ids
```

 – A comma-separated list of IDs for tickets a user must purchase to see the protected content. If left blank, all tickets for a given event will be displayed.
- ```
not_ticket_ids
```

 – A comma-separated list of IDs for tickets that should be excluded when checking if protected content should be displayed for a user. In other words, this ensures that only attendees who have purchased other tickets for the event will see the protected content. If left blank, no IDs will be evaluated.
- ```
ticketed
```

text:
## Ticket examples

#### Example 1: Protected content based on any attendee for the current event

```
[tribe_tickets_protected_content]
This content will only show to attendees of the current event this shortcode is embedded on.
[/tribe_tickets_protected_content]

```
[tribe_tickets_protected_content post_id="123"]
This content will only show to attendees of the event (ID: 123).

Where 123 is the ID of the post/page/event where the tickets were created.

[/tribe_tickets_protected_content]

page_title: Understanding Provisional Event IDs in The Events Calendar
heading_path: Understanding Provisional Event IDs in The Events Calendar
text:
In The Events Calendar, especially when working with recurring events or the custom tables system, you may encounter an ID that looks like a Post ID but is much larger (e.g., 
```
10000114
```

). This is a **provisional ID**, and it refers to a specific *occurrence* of an event, not the parent event post itself.

This guide explains what these IDs are and how to correctly convert them to their corresponding WordPress 
```
post->ID
```

.

page_title: Understanding Provisional Event IDs in The Events Calendar
text:
## What is a Provisional ID?

The Events Calendar uses a custom table system (
```
wp_tec_occurrences
```

) to efficiently store and query individual instances of events, particularly for recurring event series. This system generates its own unique IDs for each occurrence to ensure high performance.

A provisional ID is the unique identifier for a single event occurrence within these custom tables. It is **not** the same as the standard WordPress Post ID for the 
```
tribe_events
```

 post type.

You will most likely encounter these IDs when:

- Looking at the URL of a single recurring event instance.
- Querying the 
```
wp_tec_occurrences
```

 database table directly.
- Working with certain hooks and filters related to event occurrences.

page_title: Understanding Provisional Event IDs in The Events Calendar
text:
## The Problem: Mismatched IDs

Standard WordPress functions like 
```
get_post_meta()
```

, 
```
get_the_title()
```

, or 
```
get_permalink()
```

 require a standard 
```
post->ID
```

. If you pass a provisional ID to these functions, they will fail because there is no post in the 
```
wp_posts
```

 table with that ID.

page_title: Understanding Provisional Event IDs in The Events Calendar
text:
## The Solution: normalize_id()

The Events Calendar provides a safe, forward-compatible utility function to resolve a provisional ID back to its proper WordPress Post ID.

The function is a static method: 
```
TECEventsCustom_TablesV1ModelsOccurrence::normalize_id()
```

This function accepts an ID (either provisional or a standard Post ID) and will always return the correct, integer-based WordPress Post ID.

page_title: Displaying and Managing the Public Attendee List
heading_path: Displaying and Managing the Public Attendee List
text:
The Public Attendee List powers the [Who’s Attending feature](https://docs.nexcess.com/software/the-events-calendar/assigned-seating-tickets/#global-stock) on your event page while using [Event Tickets Plus](https://theeventscalendar.com/product/wordpress-event-tickets-plus/), but it can do much more. It is a list of all of the attendees for an event, allowing you and others to see who is attending the event. This is powered by the API, which is public. You can learn more about APIs in our [REST API article](https://theeventscalendar.com/knowledgebase/k/introduction-to-the-events-calendar-rest-api/).

We have combined the end-user permissions for the full Public Attendee List and the Who’s Attending block.  At this time, we do provide a way for users to opt-out from these.

page_title: Displaying and Managing the Public Attendee List
text:
## Viewing attendees

In Classic Editor mode, select Settings from the Tickets meta box then choose the option to **Show attendees list on event page**.

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/CleanShot-2023-12-16-at-12.46.14@2x.jpg)Ticket meta box in the WordPress Classic editor

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/CleanShot-2023-12-16-at-12.48.42@2x.jpg)Enable “Who’s Attending” to display on the front end of your site

If you have enabled the WordPress Block editor (a.k.a Gutenberg), you will add the **Attendee List** to your event, page, or post using the Ticket block.

![Attendee List block in the WordPress Block Editor](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Block-Editor-Add-attendees-block.jpg)The Attendee List block in the WordPress Block editor

![Public Attendee List on the front end](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Block-Editor-Attendees-block.jpg)The Attendee List block added to the post

Note: If the user opts out of being displayed on the Who’s Attending/Attendee List, they will be displayed as anonymous in the Who’s Attending block.

page_title: Displaying and Managing the Public Attendee List

## Displaying attendees

![](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-2-4.jpg)

**Important**: For the Avatars to display, you need to have Avatars enabled in **Settings > Discussion**

Once the attendee list has been enabled, visitors are able to opt into being displayed on the list during registration. You are able to display the attendees who have opted in in a variety of ways.

Some WordPress themes and plugins provide custom solutions to display attendees within widgets and sidebars. You could also integrate this with your own mobile app, other content management systems, and more.

To access all attendee registrations that are publicly available for all events on your site, go to this link on your own website:

```
[yoursite.com]/wp-json/tribe/tickets/v1/attendees/
```

To access all attendee registrations that are publicly available for just a single ticket within an event, this is the link you can use:

```

page_title: Displaying and Managing the Public Attendee List
heading_path: Opting out of the attendee list
text:
## Opting out of the attendee list

To be shown in the public attendee results, users will need to uncheck the box, allowing themselves to be publicly visible as attending the event. We have made the default option to be opt-out to comply more closely with GDPR, California Customer Privacy Act, and similar best practices.

page_title: Displaying and Managing the Public Attendee List
text:
### Hiding the attendee list option

**Note:** If you use the Who’s Attending feature on your site, but hide the opt-out question, users will be hidden from the Public Attendee List.

Since Event Tickets Plus 4.11.2, both Classic and Block users will see an opt-out form below tickets on the front end of their website. Previously, this feature was only displayed within the RSVP Block (not Classic mode).

![Opting out of the public attendee list](https://docs.nexcess.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-13.jpg)By default, users will be opted-out of the Public Attendee API.

**Note:** You can hide the opt-out form so users do not need to opt-in or opt-out of being displayed in the list. However, this makes complying with GDPR and other policies more complex. Proceed with caution.

Add this CSS snippet to your theme’s styles (or use a style override) to hide the option:

```
.tribe-tickets-attendees-list-optout--wrapper {
    display: none !important;
}
```

It’s also possible to hide the option using the 
```
tribe_tickets_plus_hide_attendees_list_optout
```

 filter in your 
```
functions.php
```

 file or as a separate plugin.
